title: Mayville freshman Brielle Ehlers breaks school record in playoff win - NewsBreak
text:
By Ben Schultz ,
23 hours ago
BERLIN – Outside the Berlin High School gym, a fresh coat of snow covered cars and the roads.
It even slowed an officials drive, as Mayville and Berlin lined up ready for their first-round playoff matchup. The ref was late, but made it quickly after the original start time of 7 p.m.
While the ref may not have been ready, the Mayville girls basketball team, with three freshmen in the starting lineup, were.
Mayville picked up its first playoff win since the 2020-21 season when it defeated Campbellsport. On Tuesday, Feb. 24 it beat Berlin, 53-32.
“It’s fantastic. We talk about legacy for our seniors, for the freshman, so this is definitely a step towards building that legacy and moving into the right direction,” Mayville head coach David Beebe said.
Mayville was led by freshman Brielle Ehlers who finished with 15 points, while senior Layla Budahn finished with 14.
“I was hoping we could take advantage of them inside and I thought we really did a good job of that,” Beebe said.
Leading the way for Berlin was Aubrie Hilgart who finished with 12 points and Ahzayla Bell added 11. The loss ended the high school basketball career of four seniors, Becca Bartol, Lillian Johnson, Lakelyn Sobieski and Lauren Werch. Berlin ended the season with a 10-15 record.
“Our younger girls talked on senior night about them, the inspiration. They’re three, four, five activity type kids, they’re pillars in this community,” Berlin head coach Eric Hacker said. “I would’ve loved to have had another two, three, four days or a couple of weeks with them.”
With the win, Mayville will face its toughest test of the season. In the second round Mayville will play at 7 p.m., Friday, Feb. 27 at undefeated Oostburg.
“I think they’re the top team in the state regardless of division,” Beebe said. "If we look at this freshmen group, it’s a playoff win in their first year and then if we can stack another one and another one as we progress. I think it’s an awesome opportunity to go to an atmosphere that’s going to be great."
Here are takeaways from the game.
Mayville’s Defense The Cardinals defense was the story of the game.
Mayville came out in a box-and-1 with a diamond starting at the top of the key. Freshman Brooke Waas was tasked with guarding Berlin’s leading scorer, Sobieski who came into the game averaging 14.4 points per game.
Waas defended her the entire length of the court and gave her no room or space to move.
“It was hard, but when you have an amazing team and you have an amazing team supporting you, that’s all you need,” Waas said.
Sobieski finished the game with four points, and even when she got past Waas, she was met by a defender at the rim.
But it wasn’t just Waas.
Mayville forced 15 Berlin turnovers in the first half, a majority of which came by Ady Christian steals as she defended from the wing. Berlin finished the game with 20 turnovers to Mayville’s 18. In Christian’s freshman season she broke Mayville’s single-season record for steals and added even more against Berlin.
“It’s phenomenal what she is and what she’s capable of doing," Beebe said.
Quick Starts Mayville took an 11-3 lead to start the game, with eight of the points coming from Christian. As the half wore on Mayville took a 13-point lead, but Berlin closed the half strong and went into halftime down 26-20.
Once again, Mayville had a strong start and opened the second half with a 10-0 scoring run.
“We started to pile up some stuff in our favor in that second half and (in a) playoff game you just got to start stacking chips whenever you can and hopefully at the end of the day it comes out with your side up,” Beebe said.
School Records In the first half, Ehlers broke Mayville’s single-season blocks record. Mayville fans had signs ready to go and were ready to show them off when the record block happened.
“It’s crazy. We’ve had two freshmen break school records this year. Ady broke the school records for steals this year, now Brielle broke the school record for blocks,” Beebe said. “I think it just shows their potential and what they’re able to accomplish.”
Sobieski ended her season with a school record for 3-pointers made in a season with 65.
“It’s a neat milestone. Lakelyn’s a talented kid, three-sport athlete, she works hard. She did a lot of really good things this year,” Hacker said.
